Use a **partial update**: accept a `PATCH` request with a model whose fields are all optional, then apply only the fields the user actually sent.

**Why this matters:** If you replace the whole record with `PUT`, any field the client leaves out falls back to the model's default. In the docs' example, a body that omits the stored `"tax": 20.2` means the input model would take the default value of `"tax": 10.5`.[5] With the HTTP `PATCH` operation[5], you can send only the data that you want to update, leaving the rest intact.[5]

**Steps:**
1. **Make every field optional.** If you want to receive partial updates that can omit all the attributes, you need to have a model with all the attributes marked as optional (with default values or `None`).[3] You can keep this update model separate from your create model, which has required fields, by following [Extra Models](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/extra-models/).
2. **Load the stored data** and put it in a Pydantic model.
3. **Keep only the fields that were sent.** Use `exclude_unset`, like `item.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`.[5] This lets you update only the values actually set by the user, instead of overriding values already stored with default values in your model.[3]
4. **Merge and save.** Create a copy of the stored model, updating its attributes with the received partial updates (using the `update` parameter).[3] Then save it.

```python
@app.patch("/items/{item_id}")
async def update_item(item_id: str, item: Item) -> Item:
    stored_item_data = items[item_id]
    stored_item_model = Item(**stored_item_data)
    update_data = item.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    updated_item = stored_item_model.model_copy(update=update_data)
    items[item_id] = jsonable_encoder(updated_item)
    return updated_item
```

**With SQLModel**, the SQL databases tutorial applies the same idea with a `HeroUpdate` model. It has all the same fields that would be needed to create a new hero, but all the fields are optional[1]:

```python
hero_data = hero.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
hero_db.sqlmodel_update(hero_data)
session.add(hero_db)
session.commit()
```

You don't have to use `PATCH`. You can actually use this same technique with an HTTP `PUT` operation.[3]
